purpose: Crosswalk the global dataset's Cagayan drainage-basin geometry with independently sourced locality evidence and a bounded GBIF coordinate search. This is not a complete Cagayan fish inventory.

basinGeometry.interpretation: A northern Luzon drainage-basin polygon. It is not Cagayan de Misamis in Mindanao, a municipal boundary, or a coastal municipal-water boundary.

attributeCentroid.note: Dataset attribute centroid, not a verified sampling locality.

geometry.method: Downloaded the four basin shapefile components to ignored temporary storage and matched the DBF record B0380 to the polygon record. Candidate points were checked against the polygon rings with an even-odd point-in-polygon test; the input files were checksum-verified against the Zenodo API metadata. The polygon was not copied into the app or repository.

candidateSet.meaning: These names are source-dataset basin-level candidates. The extract's referenceIds are taxonomic-bibliography identifiers, not a verified citation-to-basin crosswalk.

queryParameters.taxa: Each of the eight candidate names was queried separately. A strict species match/taxon key was used where available; otherwise an exact scientific-name query was used. The bounding-box screen is broader than the polygon; positive coordinates were separately checked against B0380.

results.duplicateFeedRecord: AB469437 appears once in the NCBI-mined feed and once in the INSDC Sequences feed.
results.localityInterpretation: GBIF rows report Luzon/Cagayan River-system text, but all 36 rows share the same coarse coordinate. The DDBJ source accession AB469437 independently records the same shared point and a 2008-02-08 collection date, but supplies no physical voucher/catalog number or exact sampling reach. This is one historical sequence-locality lead, not 36 independent specimen locations or a precise station. A GBIF example is https://www.gbif.org/occurrence/3346179802.

results.independentLocalityEvidence: Smithsonian NMNH holotype USNM 333262 is catalogued from Intel River, a pool at Barangay Hot Springs, Baggao, Cagayan; collection date 1989-05-05. The record has no coordinate used in this overlay, so it is a historical textual voucher locality, not a point-in-polygon result.

results.interpretation: The six GBIF rows represent two museum catalog numbers duplicated across occurrence/material-sample feed records. Market coordinates and vendor-reported nearby catch areas do not establish precise capture stations or a verified basin occurrence.

results.gbifSpeciesMatch: No exact GBIF species-rank match in the reviewed query.
results.interpretation: The basin candidate remains unresolved pending direct review of the 2024 original description and its specimen/type-locality details. Third-party name summaries were not promoted to locality evidence.

A zero-result bounded search does not establish absence. Follow-up to the original 2005 description and type series is documented in national-freshwater-cagayan-stigmatogobius-elegans-imurung-type-locality-20261106.json; its locality remains uncoordinated and is not yet polygon-matched to B0380.

The bounded query under GBIF usage key 2377266 returned zero coordinates. The current Catalog of Fishes and 2023 revision treat S. kyphosus as a synonym of S. genivittatus, while GBIF still marks it accepted. Reviewed historical localities are Camiguin, Mindanao, and Leyte; no source ties this candidate to Cagayan. This is an unresolved discovery-association and taxonomy mismatch, not absence evidence.

updatedTaxonomicCrosswalk.catalogStatus: Synonym of Stenogobius genivittatus (Valenciennes, 1837), citing Causse et al. 2023:154; GBIF still accepts S. kyphosus under usage key 2377266.
updatedTaxonomicCrosswalk.localityFinding: Reviewed original type records and 2023 revision list Camiguin, Mindanao, and Leyte localities; no Cagayan locality was found. The B0380 discovery candidate remains unvalidated.
updatedTaxonomicCrosswalk.caveat: Taxonomic-source disagreement and a bounded zero result do not establish presence or absence in Cagayan.

results.gbifSpeciesMatch: Higher-rank match only; exact-name query returned zero species-rank records in the screen.
results.interpretation: A separate Glossogobius giuris market record is not G. biorbitalis. Its vendor-reported Northern Cagayan vicinity and market-geocoded coordinate do not establish either species identity or a precise natural capture locality.

results.independentTypeLocalityEvidence: The California Academy of Sciences Primary Types Imagebase gives the holotype locality as Cagayan de Misamis, Misamis Oriental, Mindanao.
results.interpretation: The shared place-name Cagayan creates a basin-name ambiguity for this Luzon candidate; the Mindanao type locality does not prove the taxon is absent from northern Luzon. No zero-result inference is made.

limitations: A rectangular query window is not a polygon query; only returned coordinates were tested against the basin polygon.
GBIF coordinate rows can be duplicated across datasets or feed representations and may georeference a market or generalized locality rather than a collection station.
Missing, higher-rank, or zero-result matches do not prove taxonomic or biological absence.
A basin association and a historical type locality do not imply continuous, current, or fishable distribution throughout the basin.

interpretation: The dataset's B0380 Cagayan geometry is a northern Luzon drainage-basin polygon; the identical place-name in Cagayan de Misamis is in Mindanao and is a separate locality.

The strongest independently localized leads in this screen are the textual USNM 333262 type locality for Nomorhamphus rossi and the historical sequence locality for Anguilla luzonensis. Only the eel's coarse shared coordinate was tested within the polygon; it is not a precise sampling reach.
The market-based Mugil and Glossogobius records remain vendor-vicinity claims, not exact basin collection localities.

The eight-name basin candidate set remains discovery-only and incomplete. Review each taxon's underlying primary source separately and keep Cagayan River reaches, tributaries, lakes, reservoirs, and administrative areas distinct.

disposition.reason: This review resolves a source geometry identifier and screens locality evidence; it does not provide sufficiently precise, independently licensed public occurrence rows or exact waterbody geometry for the app.
